notes: rust-stdlib-crypto over the reviewed rsa (0.10.0-rc.19), crypto-bigint and crypto-primes crates; the rsa crate carries RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (Marvin timing attack on private-key operations, no patched release), recorded in docs/crypto-dependencies.json, ADR 0003 and the module documentation. *big.Int fields are bigint::Int and E is i64. hash.Hash arguments (OAEP) are crypto::Hash identifiers because the crate selects digests by type. OAEP encryption and PSS signing honour the supplied reader as Go does; GenerateKey and EncryptPKCS1v15 ignore it like Go 1.26+ unless GODEBUG=cryptocustomrand=1, and GODEBUG=rsa1024min=0 allows keys below 1024 bits. PrivateKey implements crypto::Signer and crypto::Decrypter; PKCS #1, PKCS #8 and PKIX DER hooks serve x509.

DecryptOAEP.note: takes a crypto::Hash in place of a hash.Hash instance; supported pairs are documented in the module; Go ignores the reader argument, so there is no rng parameter.

DecryptPKCS1v15.note: Go ignores the reader argument, so there is no rng parameter.

DecryptPKCS1v15SessionKey.note: same results as Go but not constant time: Go's Bleichenbacher countermeasure is a first-party construction (ADR 0003); Go ignores the reader argument, so there is no rng parameter.

EncryptOAEP.note: takes a crypto::Hash in place of a hash.Hash instance; Go's reader argument becomes `rsa::encrypt_oaep_with_rng`, which takes the reader first; the plain function uses the system source (ADR 0005). Go always honours the reader.

EncryptOAEPWithOptions.note: Go's reader argument becomes `rsa::encrypt_oaep_with_options_and_rng`, which takes the reader first; the plain function uses the system source (ADR 0005). Go always honours the reader.

EncryptPKCS1v15.note: Go's reader argument becomes `rsa::encrypt_pkcs1v15_with_rng`, which takes the reader first; the plain function uses the system source (ADR 0005). Go 1.26+ ignores the reader unless GODEBUG=cryptocustomrand=1.

GenerateKey.note: Go's reader argument becomes `rsa::generate_key_with_rng`, which takes the reader first; the plain function uses the system source (ADR 0005). Go 1.26+ ignores the reader unless GODEBUG=cryptocustomrand=1.

GenerateMultiPrimeKey.note: two-prime keys only: the rsa crate loads and uses multi-prime keys but does not expose generating them; Go's reader argument becomes `rsa::generate_multi_prime_key_with_rng`, which takes the reader first; the plain function uses the system source (ADR 0005). Go 1.26+ ignores the reader unless GODEBUG=cryptocustomrand=1.

PrivateKey.Decrypt.note: rand and opts are optional (Go passes nil); Go ignores the reader argument, so there is no rng parameter. opts is optional (Go passes nil).

PrivateKey.Equal.note: takes &dyn Any in place of crypto.PrivateKey

PrivateKey.Sign.note: sign is Go's Sign(nil, ...); sign_with_rng reads the PSS salt from the reader (PKCS #1 v1.5 ignores it, as in Go)

PublicKey.Equal.note: takes &dyn Any in place of crypto.PublicKey

SignPKCS1v15.note: None is Go's zero crypto.Hash; Go ignores the reader argument, so there is no rng parameter.

SignPSS.note: Go's reader argument becomes `rsa::sign_pss_with_rng`, which takes the reader first; the plain function uses the system source (ADR 0005). Go always honours the reader.
